marks.label: Week 10: 230
marks.ask: How do you find the nth term of an arithmetic sequence?

explain.say: Meet Ama in Accra. She starts a savings pot with 50 cedis, and every week she adds 20 more. Look at the yellow mark: in week 1 the pot has 50 cedis.

draw.text: Saving the same each week: arithmetic sequences

marks.label: Week 10: 230
marks.ask: How do you find the nth term of an arithmetic sequence?

explain.say: Each week adds the same 20, so the list goes 50, 70, 90, 110, 130. A list that grows by the same amount each time is called an arithmetic sequence. The 20 is the common difference. What is in the pot in week 5?

marks.label: Week 10: 230
marks.ask: How do you find the nth term of an arithmetic sequence?

explain.say: 130 cedis! Look at the cyan mark. Because the same amount is added every week, the points sit on a straight line. The slope of that line is the common difference, 20.

marks.label: Week 10: 230
marks.ask: How do you find the nth term of an arithmetic sequence?

explain.say: Here is a shortcut. To reach week n you add 20 a total of n minus 1 times. So term n is 50 plus n minus 1 times 20. For week 10: 50 plus 9 times 20 is 230. Look at the purple mark.

marks.label: Week 10: 230
marks.ask: How do you find the nth term of an arithmetic sequence?

explain.say: Well done! Challenge: in which week does Ama's pot first pass 500 cedis? Use the formula and see. Rent rises, taxi fares and seats in a stadium often follow arithmetic sequences too.

faq.a: A list of numbers where you add the same amount each time, like 50, 70, 90, 110. The amount added is the common difference.

faq.q: How do you find the nth term of an arithmetic sequence?
faq.a: Use first term plus n minus 1 times the common difference. For 50, 70, 90, the nth term is 50 plus n minus 1 times 20.
asks: What is the formula for the nth term?

faq.q: Why does an arithmetic sequence make a straight line?
faq.a: Because each step adds the same amount, the graph goes up by the same height each time. Equal steps give a straight line.

faq.q: In which week does the pot first pass 500 cedis?
faq.a: Solve 50 plus n minus 1 times 20 is more than 500. Then n minus 1 must be more than 22.5, so week 24, with 510 cedis.

faq.q: Can the common difference be negative?
faq.a: Yes. If you take away the same amount each time, like 100, 93, 86, the common difference is minus 7 and the line slopes down.
asks: What is a decreasing arithmetic sequence?

facts: The nth term of an arithmetic sequence is a + (n − 1)d, where a is the first term and d the common difference.

quiz.say: What is the common difference of 7, 11, 15, 19, …?
quiz.show: What is the common difference of 7, 11, 15, 19, …?
quiz.why: Each term is 4 more than the last.

wrong.1: 7 is the first term, not the difference.

wrong.0: 100 multiplies 20 by 5, using n instead of n − 1.
wrong.2: 103 adds 20 lots of 5 to the first term, one step too many.
